title: Named Routes, Route Groups aur Special Routes
objectives: Named routes banana aur `route()`/`redirect()->route()` se use karna
Route cache ka basic idea jaanna

sections.heading: Named routes
sections.body: Route ko naam do aur URL kabhi hardcode mat karo. Kal URL badla to sirf route definition badalni padegi.
explain: Extra array keys query string ban jaati hain (`?page=2`).
`request()->routeIs('products.*')` se current route check kar sakte ho.

sections.heading: Real-world example: Admin panel
sections.body: Admin ke saare routes ka URL `/admin/...` se shuru hota hai aur route naam `admin.` se. Har route par yeh dohrane ki jagah group use karo.
explain: `name('admin.')` – route ke naam ke aage `admin.` lagata hai.
Group mein `->middleware('auth')` bhi laga sakte ho (Authentication module mein seekhenge).

sections.heading: Controller group aur special routes
sections.body: Same controller ke routes ek group mein likh sakte ho. Kuch aur kaam ke routes:
explain: `Route::controller()` – group ke saare routes ke liye ek controller.
`Route::redirect` – seedha redirect, controller ki zarurat nahi.
`match([...])` – kuch chune hue methods. `any` – saare methods.
`fallback` – koi bhi route match na ho to chalta hai. Ise hamesha sabse last mein rakho.

sections.heading: Route cache
sections.body: Production mein routes ko cache karne se application tez chalti hai. Cache ke liye saare routes controller-based hone chahiye (closure routes cache nahi hote).

code.code:
php artisan route:cache
php artisan route:clear

callout.text: Development mein `route:cache` mat chalao, warna route badalne par asar nahi dikhega. Dikhe nahi to `php artisan route:clear` chalao.

versionDiff.heading: Version notes
versionDiff.intro: Named routes aur groups teeno versions mein same hain. Farak API routes ki file mein hai.

items.11: `routes/api.php` default mein nahi hota. `php artisan install:api` se banta hai, aur uske routes par `/api` prefix lagta hai.
items.13: Same as 11. Groups, `Route::controller()` aur `fallback` same kaam karte hain.

errors.cause: Group mein `->middleware('auth')` lagaya par login route abhi bana hi nahi, to auth middleware redirect nahi kar pata.
errors.fix: Authentication module tak `auth` middleware mat lagao, ya `login` naam ka route banao.

errors.cause: Group mein `name('admin.')` lagaya par route par `->name('dashboard')` nahi hai, ya naam alag hai.
errors.fix: Poora naam `route:list` se dekho: prefix + route ka naam.

errors.error: Fallback route sab kuch pakad raha hai
errors.fix: Fallback ko file ke bilkul end mein rakho.

debug.body: Naam aur URL ka poora mapping `route:list` mein dikhta hai.

code.code:
php artisan route:list --name=admin
php artisan route:list --except-vendor

tasks: `admin` prefix aur `admin.` naam ke saath group banao
Sabse end mein ek `fallback` route banao jo custom 404 message de

quiz.q: `Route::prefix('admin')->name('admin.')` ka route naam `dashboard` ho to poora naam?
quiz.why: Prefix naam ke aage jud jaata hai: `admin.dashboard`.
Fallback sirf tab chalta hai jab koi route match na kare, isliye last mein.

quiz.q: Route cache ke liye kya zaroori hai?
options: Closure routes na hon, controller-based hon
quiz.why: Closure routes cache nahi hote, controller routes hote hain.

interview.a: URL hardcode nahi karna padta. URL badalne par sirf route definition badalti hai.

interview.q: Route group kyun use karte hain?
interview.a: Common cheezein (prefix, name, middleware, controller) ek baar likhne ke liye.
`Route::redirect` route file mein hi chhota redirect define karta hai. `redirect()` controller ke andar response ke roop mein use hota hai.
Aisa route jo tab chalta hai jab koi aur route match na kare, custom 404 ke liye.
Production deployment mein, performance ke liye. Closure routes ho to fail hota hai.

summary: Named routes URL hardcode hone se bachate hain.
Groups prefix, name, middleware aur controller share karte hain.
`route:cache` sirf production mein, closure routes ke bina.
